rgb: Across the five frames, the egocentric camera points steeply downward at an outdoor surface covered in gravel and stones; only the first frame contains a narrow glimpse of sky and sloping terrain along the upper-right edge. Roughly 1.0 to 1.5 metres ahead of the camera wearer stands another person in brown strappy sandals, visible solely from their bare lower legs to their feet near the frame top. Their torso and head are entirely cropped above the upper edge, so their gaze cannot be directly observed. Their feet point broadly toward the camera wearer with a slight angle toward the camera’s left. The wearer’s forearms, hands, and blue-shoed right foot fill the lower foreground, about 0.5 to 0.8 metres beneath the camera. From frames 1 to 3, the camera tilts farther down and approaches the ground, moving the other person’s feet into the upper-left quadrant and placing the stones and shell pieces immediately before the wearer’s right foot within arm’s reach. During frames 3 and 4, the wearer reaches their right hand forward and downward to the ground approximately 0.4 to 0.6 metres beyond their right foot, while the left hand remains low on the left beside a flat white shell fragment. By frame 5, the right hand has lifted into the right foreground, around 0.25 to 0.35 metres from the lens, holding a small white object that partly blocks the gravel behind it.
depth: The monocular depth visualization shows an outdoor rocky ground plane viewed from above on a slope, approximately 0.5–1.5 m beneath the camera. At the bottom are the camera wearer’s forearms, hands, and blue-shoed right leg, rendered brightest and lying roughly 0.2–0.8 m away. Another person’s lower legs and sandal-wearing feet appear ahead in the upper-left, about 1.2–1.8 m from the camera and around 0.8–1.2 m from the wearer’s feet. Neither person’s head or upper body is visible because both are cropped out. The other person’s feet face forward with a slight rightward angle relative to the wearer, and the ground directly below contains pebbles plus a small round white stone handled within arm’s reach, approximately 0.2–0.6 m away. Through the five frames, the wearer crouches or bends lower, extending the right hand toward the ground at about 0.6 m in frames 3–4 before raising the stone near the lens on the right at roughly 0.25 m in frame 5. Meanwhile, the other person’s legs move toward the top-left boundary and become darker in the depth rendering. Relative to RGB, this map more clearly distinguishes the vertical elevation of the wearer’s raised right arm and leg from the similarly textured rocky surface. However, it is unreliable around the outer fisheye corners, which become black, and in frame 5, where the other person’s feet almost disappear into the background depth gradient.
segmentation: The instance-segmentation view separates the foreground human limbs from the unlabelled stony terrain. It locates the other person’s feet and lower legs in the upper-left, roughly 1.2–1.8 m away and oriented toward the camera wearer’s right, while the wearer’s hands, forearms, and right leg occupy the bottom at about 0.2–0.8 m away and within arm’s reach. Because both people’s heads and torsos fall outside the image, their gaze cannot be inferred from the masks. Foot direction nevertheless indicates that the wearer faces forward and downward toward the other person’s legs, which are approximately 0.8–1.2 m ahead. Across all five frames, the other person’s leg mask withdraws toward the upper-left image boundary as the wearer’s right arm reaches forward to the ground in frames 3–4, then lifts along the right side in frame 5. In that last frame, the small white stone held between the fingers receives a segmentation mask and is classified as a 'sports ball' at about 0.25 m distance. Compared with RGB alone, the map makes the held object’s precise outline and the limb edges easier to distinguish from the densely scattered pebbles. Its output is nonetheless unreliable because it divides the wearer’s own body parts into several separate 'person' instances, assigns them inconsistent colours, and produces straight horizontal truncations across the right forearm in frames 4–5.
pose: The pose visualization contains only magenta two-dimensional hand skeletons against black, tracking the camera wearer’s hands in the lower foreground at approximately 0.2–0.6 m distance and within immediate reaching range, while leaving out every body skeleton, leg, foot, and feature of the rocky ground. Frame 1 shows only the wearer’s overlapping hands at the bottom-left, around 0.4 m away. Frames 2 and 4 track both hands: the left appears at the bottom-left near 0.5 m, and the right lies at the bottom-centre/right about 0.5–0.6 m away, with roughly 0.2–0.3 m separating them. Frame 3 contains only the left hand, whereas frame 5 contains solely the elevated right hand at middle-right, approximately 0.25 m away. Heavy cropping keeps the upper bodies and heads outside the frames and prevents detection of the other person’s legs, which are about 1.2–1.8 m ahead in the upper-left. Consequently, this map alone cannot establish gaze or facing direction. Over the sequence, the visible skeletons trace the right hand reaching forward toward the ground, then rising and spreading its fingers toward the camera in frame 5. Fine finger positioning and the pinching posture are therefore much more legible here than in the RGB sequence, although the result is unreliable because it misses the reaching right hand entirely in frame 3 and fails to detect the left hand in frame 5.
